title: StochasticCompositeHessianLipschitz.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Minimize F=f+ψ over convex Q; f may be nonconvex. F(x0)−F(x)≤Δ for every x∈Q.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: Smooth f plus ψ convex on Q, with an exact constrained proximal minimizer available.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Fresh IID samples give unbiased g(x,ω) with E‖g(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ². No samplewise smoothness or sample reuse is supplied.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact minimizer over Q of ‖u−z‖²/(2a)+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u), for every a>0. Gradient and proximal queries consume the same fixed oracle budget.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform finite second-moment noise bound σ²; σ≥0. No light-tail assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: ∇f is L-Lipschitz and its derivative is ρ-Lipschitz in operator norm, with L>0 and ρ≥0. L,ρ,σ,Δ,ε,x0 are public; f,ψ,Q and their oracle realizations are hidden.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The gradient-mapping norm is integrable and its expectation over algorithm and oracle randomness is at most ε.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The measurable output belongs to Q almost surely.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: E‖G_L(X)‖≤ε, where G_L(x)=L(x−prox(1/L,x,∇f(x))) and ε>0; the norm is unsquared.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Standard stochastic nonconvex composite optimization with exact proximal access, IID bounded-variance gradients, Lipschitz Hessians, and expected gradient-mapping stationarity.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Composite Stationarity

We consider minimizing F=f+ψ over a convex set Q in a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The possibly nonconvex function f:E→R has an L-Lipschitz gradient and a ρ-Lipschitz Hessian, with L>0 and ρ≥0, while ψ:E→R is convex on Q. A given x0∈Q has objective gap at most Δ≥0. The oracle returns unbiased stochastic gradients with variance at most σ2, σ≥0, from independent identically distributed samples, or exact proximal minimizers Ta(z,v) of ∥u−z∥2/(2a)+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u) over u∈Q, for a>0 and z,v∈E. For ε>0, the goal is a feasible output x¯ with E∥L(x¯−T1/L(x¯,∇f(x¯)))∥≤ε.

The optimization problem is minx∈QF(x),F(x):=f(x)+ψ(x). The norm is induced by the inner product on E; operator norms below are the induced operator norms. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, L, ρ, σ, Δ, ε, and x0, and accesses the objective through the oracle described below.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Gradient and Hessian regularity). The function f is Fréchet differentiable on E, its gradient is Fréchet differentiable on E, and, for every x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥. Here ∇2f(x) is a linear operator from E to E.

Assumption 2 (Convex composite term and proximal access). The set Q⊆E is convex, and, for every x,y∈Q and t∈[0,1], ψ((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)ψ(x)+tψ(y). For every a>0 and z,v∈E, the exact proximal reply satisfies Ta(z,v)∈Q,Ta(z,v)∈argminu∈Q{∥u−z∥22a+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u)}. The map on R×E×E equal to Ta(z,v) when a>0 and to 0 otherwise is measurable.

Assumption 3 (Initial objective gap). The given starting point and gap bound satisfy x0∈Q,F(x0)−F(x)≤Δfor every x∈Q.

Assumption 4 (Stochastic gradient access). There is a probability measure μ on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For each x∈E, the random vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable under ξ∼μ, with Eξ∼μ[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼μ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2≤σ2. The oracle samples form a measurable, mutually independent sequence (ξk)k≥0 with common law μ, under a joint probability law P on ΩN. This sequence is independent of the algorithm’s internal randomness. At call k, a gradient query at any x∈E returns g(x,ξk); a proximal query returns Ta(z,v) exactly. Each query of either type counts as one oracle call in a common budget. Proximal queries may use any real a, although the minimization and measurability conditions above concern positive a.

Define the composite gradient mapping by GL(x):=L(x−T1/L(x,∇f(x))). After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its residual norm ∥GL(x¯)∥ must be integrable, and it must satisfy x¯∈QP-a.s.,EP[∥GL(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s internal randomness and the independent oracle sample sequence.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, minimize F=f+ψ on convex Q, with x0∈Q, F(x0)−infQF≤Δ, convex ψ on Q, and measurable exact proximal evaluations. Globally, ∇f is L-Lipschitz and ∇2f is ρ-Lipschitz. The jointly measurable IID oracle is unbiased with integrable gradients and centered second moment at most σ2. Here L,ε>0 and ρ,σ,Δ≥0. Target: a measurable feasible output with ∫∥GL(xτ(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε; P includes sampling and output randomization.

(1): noise term smaller by L/ρε when ρε≪L2; total gain when noise dominates, σ≳ε, and initialization does not dominate. (1) needs global Hessian regularity and known ρ; noise term worsens if ρε>L2. Loses squared subgradient stationarity.
(3) NIGT (Cutkosky and Mehta 2020), Theorem 3 O(1+LΔε2+ρΔσ2ε7/2+σ13/3Δ4/3ρ2/3ε7/3) gradient calls; ψ=0, Q=E, Δ,ρ,σ>0. (1): Scope extends to convex composite penalties and constrained, possibly unbounded Q. Matches leading deterministic and noise terms on the overlap. (1): remaining terms incomparable. On ψ=0, Q=E, the prox is a closed-form update.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticCompositeHessianLipschitz

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE Params.borelE
  Params.measurableΩ

inductive Query (p : Params) where
  | gradient (x : p.E)
  | prox (a : ℝ) (z v : p.E)

structure Instance (p : Params) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  grad : p.E → p.E
  hess : p.E → (p.E →L[ℝ] p.E)
  ψ : p.E → ℝ
  Q : Set p.E
  prox : ℝ → p.E → p.E → p.E

noncomputable def objective {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (x : p.E) : ℝ := I.f x + I.ψ x

noncomputable def proxObjective {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (a : ℝ) (z v u : p.E) : ℝ :=
  ‖u - z‖ ^ 2 / (2 * a) + ⟪v, u - z⟫ + I.ψ u

noncomputable def gradientMapping {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (x : p.E) : p.E :=
  p.L • (x - I.prox (1 / p.L) x (I.grad x))

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Query
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (μ : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (μ : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, query) ω => match query with
              | .gradient x => g x ω
              | .prox a z v => I.prox a z v } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.f (I.grad x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖I.grad x - I.grad y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, HasFDerivAt I.grad (I.hess x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖I.hess x - I.hess y‖ ≤ q.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      Convex ℝ I.Q ∧ ConvexOn ℝ I.Q I.ψ ∧
      Measurable (fun t : ℝ × q.E × q.E => if 0 < t.1 then I.prox t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 else 0) ∧
      (∀ a, 0 < a → ∀ z v, I.prox a z v ∈ I.Q ∧
        IsMinOn (proxObjective I a z v) I.Q (I.prox a z v)) ∧
      q.x0 ∈ I.Q ∧
      (∀ x ∈ I.Q, objective I q.x0 - objective I x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (μ : Measure _)) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(μ : Measure _) = I.grad x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - I.grad x‖ ^ 2) (μ : Measure _)) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - I.grad x‖ ^ 2 ∂(μ : Measure _) ≤ q.σ ^ 2)
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), output ω ∈ I.Q) ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradientMapping I (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradientMapping I (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticCompositeHessianLipschitz
